title: Nonflat coefficient mates and normalization for ordinary etale adjoints
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption on $Y$, and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. 
For a homomorphism $C\to D$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, put $F_C=Rp_{f,*,C}j_!$ and $F_D=Rp_{f,*,D}j_!$ on the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories. Fix adjunctions $F_C\dashv g_C$, $F_D\dashv g_D$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Use derived scalar extension $T^W=-\otimes_C^LD$ and exact restriction $U^W$ with their canonical adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], and the projection $q:T^YF_C\cong F_DT^X$ of [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $U^Xg_D\cong g_CU^Y$. The natural transformation $b:T^Xg_C\to g_DT^Y$ specified by
$$\epsilon_D\circ F_Db=T^Y\epsilon_C\circ q_{g_C}^{-1}$$
is an isomorphism, including when $C\to D$ is a nonflat quotient. Under the restriction identification, $Ub$ is the constant-tensor map $D\otimes_C^Lg_CM\to g_C(D\otimes_C^LM)$, with the counit normalization of [lem-pur-etale-exceptional-constant-tensor]. These statements are natural on the whole unbounded categories and independent of resolutions.

For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $O=\mathcal O_E$, a nonzero nonunit $t\in O$, and $A_n=O/(t^n)$, let $F_A=Rp_{f,A,*}j_{!,A}\dashv G_A$ be an adjunction on strict systems. Suppose it has the evaluated adjunction and transition identifications of [lem-pur-etale-system-evaluation-bound]. If $M$ is normalized, meaning every $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible, then $G_AM$ is normalized in this same sense [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. This assertion uses the actual reduction mates $b_{m,n}$ and imposes no false flatness hypothesis on the quotient maps.

proof.text:
Write $r:U^YF_D\xrightarrow{\sim}F_CU^X$ for the single-ring restriction comparison. For $H\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},D)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ the given adjunctions and $q_K$ give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_C(K,U^Xg_DH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(T^XK,g_DH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(F_DT^XK,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(T^YF_CK,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(F_CK,U^YH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(K,g_CU^YH).$$
Let $\rho_H:U^Xg_DH\to g_CU^YH$ be the image of the identity under this bijection at $K=U^Xg_DH$. The inverse bijection applied to the other identity gives an inverse: naturality in $K$ identifies the two composites with identities. Naturality in $H$ gives a natural isomorphism $\rho$. The scalar-unit normalization of $q$ says its coefficient transpose is $r^{-1}\circ F_C(\eta^X)$, where $\eta^W$ is the scalar-extension unit. Consequently the displayed Hom bijection sends $a:K\to U^Xg_DH$ to the $F_C\dashv g_C$ adjunct of $U^Y\epsilon_{D,H}\circ r_{g_DH}^{-1}\circ F_C(a)$. Indeed scalar-transposing $\epsilon_D\circ F_D(a^\sharp)\circ q_K$ gives this composite: use $U(a^\sharp)\eta^X_K=a$ and naturality of $r$. At $a=1$ this proves
$$\epsilon_{C,U^YH}\circ F_C(\rho_H)=U^Y\epsilon_{D,H}\circ r_{g_DH}^{-1}.$$ Lean implementation: conjugateIsoEquiv for the composite scalar/geometric adjunctions gives rho; iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and the single-ring scalar-unit normalization prove its counit identity.

source.place: Proposition 2.29(2) and Construction 2.26; identify the restricted coefficient projection with its constant-tensor map

proof.text:
Define $b_M$ by the displayed $F_D\dashv g_D$ transpose in the statement, equivalently by the mate construction. Put $w_M=\rho_{T^YM}\circ U^X(b_M)$. Apply $F_C$ and the $C$-counit. The counit equation for $\rho$ from step 1, naturality of $r$ at $b_M$, and the defining transpose equation for $b_M$ give, in order,
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_C\circ F_C(w_M)
&=U^Y\epsilon_D\circ r_{g_DT^YM}^{-1}\circ F_CU^X(b_M)\\
&=U^Y(\epsilon_D\circ F_D(b_M))\circ r_{T^Xg_CM}^{-1}\\
&=U^Y(T^Y\epsilon_{C,M})\circ U^Y(q_{g_CM}^{-1})\circ r_{T^Xg_CM}^{-1}\\
&=(D_Y\otimes_C^L\epsilon_{C,M})\circ P_{g_CM}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses step 2 and naturality of its tensor identification. This last expression is exactly the counit transpose specifying the constant-tensor map $c_M:D_X\otimes_C^Lg_CM\to g_C(D_Y\otimes_C^LM)$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives $w_M=c_M$, proving the asserted map normalization.

source.place: Construction 2.26, equation (2.26.1), and Proposition 2.29(2); explicit counit calculation

proof.text: The constant-tensor theorem applies with $V=D\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$, without any finite-projective-dimension assumption, so $c_M$ is invertible. Since $\rho$ is invertible, step 3 implies $U^X(b_M)$ is invertible. Restriction is conservative here directly from its definition: the underlying abelian sheaf of each cohomology of the cone of $b_M$ is unchanged by scalar restriction. If the restricted cone is acyclic, these same cohomology sheaves are zero before restriction, so $b_M$ is an isomorphism. This uses no flatness of $C\to D$. The adjunctions, projection and tensor comparisons used above are natural transformations on unbounded derived categories; their transposes and composites are therefore natural there and independent of resolutions. In particular this is not an inference that the mate of an arbitrary isomorphism is invertible.

source.place: Proposition 2.29(2); apply constant tensor and exact conservative scalar restriction

proof.text:
For $m\ge n\ge1$ apply the single-ring result with $C=A_m$ and $D=A_n$. Choose the uniformizer $\varpi$ of the coefficient datum: $t=u\varpi^r$ for a unit $u$ and $r>0$, so $A_m=O/(\varpi^{rm})$ is finite. Also $|\ell|_E<1$, whence $\ell=v\varpi^e$ with $e>0$; any $s$ with $es\ge rm$ gives $\ell^s=0$ in $A_m$. Thus the single-ring hypotheses hold even when $t$ is not a uniformizer. The assumed evaluated adjunction and transition identifications give $(G_AM)_n\cong g_nM_n$ and identify its actual adjoint transition with
$$T^X_{m,n}g_mM_m\xrightarrow{b_{m,n}}g_nT^Y_{m,n}M_m\xrightarrow{g_n(t^M_{m,n})}g_nM_n.$$
The first arrow is invertible by step 4; the second is invertible because normalization of $M$ means $t^M_{m,n}$ is invertible, and functors preserve inverses. Hence every adjoint transition of $G_AM$ is invertible, which is precisely the stated definition of normalized. The evaluation statement already identifies these actual transitions compatibly with three indices, so no passage from isolated level objects to an unspecified system is involved. The case $m=n$ is included, as are zero input and empty schemes. Lean implements the actual Brown quotient mate by the evaluated exchange-mate cube, using the private helpers already proved in EtaleCoefficientSystemAdjoint, then cancels the evaluated adjoint isomorphism in the transition equation.
